action: Hydro-Québec customers: log in to the Espace client from the official site, reset your password if prompted, and never reuse it elsewhere. Ignore password-reset links in emails or texts.
date_note: Date of the public announcement; Hydro-Québec says it detected the unusual logins on October 20.
exec: Reused passwords let outsiders into about 2,500 utility customer accounts, and 1.7 million customers must now reset theirs.
plain: Hydro-Québec says someone used passwords stolen from other websites to get into nearly 2,500 customer accounts. About 1.7 million customers are being asked to change their password.
summary: Hydro-Québec says its monitoring detected unusual logins to its Espace client portal on October 20 and that nearly 2,500 customer accounts were accessed without authorization. A spokesperson said internal systems were not compromised and the intruder used email addresses and passwords already used on other sites. About 1.7 million of 2.8 million account holders are asked to reset passwords; multifactor authentication was rolled out to all customers on November 5.
title: Hydro-Québec asks 1.7 million customers to reset passwords after unauthorized account logins

validation.note: Noovo Info (CTV News translation) and Narcity Québec read; both quote Hydro-Québec spokesperson Louis-Olivier Batty. Hydro-Québec's own notice was not read. The headline's 'près de 2 millions' differs from the article's 1.7 million.
